parts.text: Which claim is correct about observing those cells?

options.text: The cells may be too small for the unaided eye, so she should use a microscope or a magnifying glass.
Her unaided eyes are enough, because an onion strip that looks clear has nothing tiny to observe.
A flat windowpane will show the cells, because any clear glass makes small things look larger.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Preeti peels a thin strip of onion and holds it up. With her unaided eyes she cannot see separate cells. Her teacher says the cells are still there.

part_answers.answer: Onion cells can be too small for the unaided eye, so a microscope or magnifying glass is needed.

teacher.key_rationale: Objects too small for the unaided eye need a microscope or magnifying glass. Clear looks and clear glass alone do not remove that need.
